fact: NGC 6752 is a globular cluster in the southern constellation Pavo, about 13,400 light-years away.
bio: N-body fits give it about 260,000 solar masses (Baumgardt's globular cluster database). NASA describes it as over 10 billion years old; a Hubble view of its core shows blue stragglers, stars that look too young and massive for a cluster this old, possibly made by collisions and mergers. Hubble photometry shows a broadened main sequence, and its red giants' colours track sodium and oxygen content, signs of more than one stellar population (Milone and colleagues, 2010).
